purpose: Non-windowed verification of Rust folder deletion/save-error notice state, copy and line layout; CoreText/Metal/modal/persistence acceptance deferred
build_consistency: final Ninja dry run reported no work to do
unit_verified_mechanisms: Rust preserves the complete irreversible-deletion warning, already-open-tabs statement, Unicode folder title and default Cancel policy. Save-error copy has only OK and no deletion/default-cancel action.
Delete admission rechecks workspace/readiness/busy state and live folder identity/type. Missing/pin/foreign targets, cancelled, duplicate and already accepted submissions produce no action.
Immediate rejection can retry; accepted admission closes notice state. Error acknowledgement remains possible after workspace/busy changes and never emits a deletion target.
Rust lays out every shaped body/error line, their complete extents and the separating gap. Empty, zero-width and saturated font metrics remain bounded.
implemented_pending_runtime_verification: CoreText CTTypesetter supplies complete UTF-8 line fragments using the same system font as the GPU text tiles, with a composed-character fallback when one cluster exceeds available width. Rust owns line placement and body/error extents; no native Label measures the body.

The notice custom view uses two native static-text AX nodes containing full body/error copy and small shared-context Metal canvases. Each line uses the existing ordinary Rust text primitive, shader and 32-byte quad ABI. Native fallback consumes the same line recipe.
Typography caches invalidate on width/font/error changes. Existing frame fingerprints skip unchanged GPU work. Error updates refresh AX names/alert events and resize through the native modal host.
Rust copy controls native modal title/button labels and default Cancel for deletion. The native host retains modal focus, button drawing, keyboard/default-button behavior and widget ownership.

A typed Delete request invokes the existing recursive deletion callback; Acknowledge short-circuits without invoking deletion. Existing opened-tab retention, asynchronous storage and rollback/error delivery remain application services. Admission is not durable storage completion.

The compiled GUI regression checks wrapped warning/AX structure, default Cancel and cancellation, changed workspace, confirmed deletion, removed target rejection and error acknowledgement. It has not been executed.
deferred_checkpoint: Run the curated 48-case Metal matrix (prior 47 plus FolderNoticesWrapPreserveCancelAndRejectStaleTargets) and all 20 Views controls, including folder creation, rename/delete and failed-write rollback.

Inspect actual CoreText line breaking and glyph output, no text loss/clipping, long Unicode titles, minimum-width/scale/theme behavior, missing-drawable fallback and native/Metal ownership transitions.
Verify native default Cancel/Enter/Escape/keyboard/AX behavior, error alert announcement, repeated/rejected/stale confirmations, modal teardown and asynchronous write failure rollback/error delivery.
Confirm already-open tabs survive folder deletion and profile/session isolation remains intact; package/sign and inspect the matching isolated app.
Measure actual CPU/GPU/presentation workload separately; no latency or speedup is established by the unit results.
limitations: CoreText shaping, native modal behavior and GPU rendering were compiled but not exercised. Rust line-layout tests consume supplied metrics and do not prove native typography or visual quality.
Native title/button controls, focus/keyboard/window lifetime and other Views surfaces remain. Full UI migration is incomplete.
Deletion and durable storage remain existing application services. Runtime persistence, rollback and opened-tab behavior still require the checkpoint.
No dependency, crate or framework was added. CoreText and the existing shader/text path were already linked; original-code Apache-2.0 and required upstream notices are unchanged.
